Quoting & estimating - AI tools for contractors

Producing estimates and bids faster — measuring, takeoffs, material pricing and proposal writing.

Why this matters Estimating is where trades lose the most unpaid hours, and a slow quote usually means a lost job.

What Quoting & estimating actually involves

Quoting is where a trade business either wins the job or spends the evening writing a bid nobody accepts. Most contractors still price from experience and a materials list, which works fine until the job is bigger than usual or the customer is comparing three quotes. The tools here range from fast estimate builders you can use on the doorstep to AI that measures drawings and produces a takeoff for you.

Frequently asked questions

Which quoting & estimating tools are worth trying first?

The three that stand out here are Joist (Solo contractors and small crews who mainly need to quote and get paid), Togal.AI (Contractors who bid from plans and spend hours on manual takeoffs), Knowify (Contractors who need to know whether a job actually made money). Start with the one that matches your size and the work you do most, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does quoting & estimating software cost?

Across the 8 tools on this page, 4 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices move often, so confirm on the vendor site before committing.

Can I try these tools for free?

Yes 鈥?Joist, ChatGPT, Claude, Grammarly all have a free tier, so you can run a few real jobs through them before paying anything.

How fast should I send a quote?

Same day is the realistic target for small jobs. On domestic work the first quote back wins far more often than the cheapest one, so a rough but fast number beats an accurate one that arrives two days later.
